title: MATLAB Quiz
description: Review the 12 starter lessons. The questions name the example to revisit. Take your time, use the lessons, and read the reason after each answer.

questions.question: disp displays a value. Single quotes can hold a row of characters. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: disp writes the character row. The semicolon avoids an extra automatic display. Use matching quotes for text.

questions.question: A variable stores a value. A semicolon hides the automatic display of an assignment. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The assignment stores 3. disp shows the sum 5. Without a semicolon MATLAB also shows the assignment result.

questions.question: Square brackets build a row vector, which is a line of values. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Brackets build a row. fprintf uses an integer slot for each value. Commas or spaces divide items in a row.

questions.question: MATLAB indexing starts at 1. Parentheses select an item. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Parentheses select the second position, which contains 5. Index zero is not allowed.

questions.question: Semicolons divide matrix rows. A cell is selected by row, then column. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The semicolon starts a new matrix row. (2,1) selects its first value, 3. Write row before column in the index.

questions.question: The dot in .* means element-by-element multiplication. Each matching pair is multiplied. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: .* multiplies corresponding positions: 2 times 4 and 3 times 5. Plain * means matrix multiplication, which is a different operation.

questions.question: The colon form start:step:end builds evenly spaced values. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The range starts at 1 and steps by 2, reaching 3 and 5. The middle number is a step size, not an item count.

questions.question: A logical test makes a true-or-false mask for selecting values. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The mask is false for 4 and true for 8 and 9. Those true positions survive. Use parentheses for indexing, not square brackets.

questions.question: mean returns the average. For this row it adds three numbers and divides by three. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The row sum is 12. mean divides it by the three values. For a matrix, check which dimension mean works along.

questions.question: if chooses a block of steps. end closes the block. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The test is true, so the Pass branch runs. Do not forget end after the if block.

questions.question: A for loop visits each value in the row after the equals sign. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The range gives n the values 1, 2 and 3. Each iteration calls fprintf. The loop variable changes each time; do not reset it inside.

questions.question: An anonymous function is a short function value. @(n) names its input. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The @ input form creates a function taking n. Calling it with 4 returns 8. Use . operators when a function should work item by item on arrays.
